newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen down 80-95 bcf in wkly AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen down 80-95 bcf in wkly AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to fall by 80-95 billion cubic feet (bcf) when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said this week.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations for a drawdown ranged from 50 bcf to 155 bcf for the week ended February 21.
While pressure is mounting to trim stocks, particularly in the East, before the March 31 end of the withdrawal season, traders said relatively mild weather last week cut demand.
"It should be a relatively low number based on last week's weather which was on the mild side," a Texas-based trader said.

In the last report, overall stocks fell by 147 bcf, well-above expectations, but were still 143 bcf, or almost 15 percent, above year-ago. Eastern storage last week stood at 233 bcf, or 51 percent, over last year. The four week average drawdown is 130 bcf.

For the same week last year, total inventories dropped by just 64 bcf, meaning a draw today in the expected range would cut the overall surplus to 1996 to about 120 bcf. Eastern storage fell by 50 bcf last year, while producing stocks dropped by nine bcf and western stocks by five bcf.
